Gauḍavaho
See Gauḍavadha.

Gauḍa
poet. Padyāmṛtataraṅgiṇī verse 100; Sūktisundara verse 159; Padyaracanā p. 23, verse 39; the verse refers to King Mukundadeva of Orissa who was killed in 1567 A. D. See Intro. to Padyāmṛtataraṅgiṇī.

Gauḍa_(?)
lex. Q. by Kṣīrasvāmin in C. on Amarakośa; also by Hemacandra in Abhidhānacintāmaṇi, Oxf. 185b an. frequently in Śabdabhedaprakāśaṭīkā of Jñānavimalagaṇi (written in 1598 A. D.), Weber 1708 (p. 265) an. used by Viśvanātha Vaidya in composing his Kośakalpataru. See Poona Ori. XIII. p. 22.

Gauḍakumbhakāra
a nickname of Abhinanda, a. of Rāmacarita.
See NCC. I. Revised edn. p. 297a. [Page218-b]

Gauḍatarka
ny. Oppert II. 7047.

Gauḍajñātyudbhava
on Gauḍa Brahmins settled in Gujarat under the patronage of King Vijayasim3ha. RASB. IV. 3103 (inc.).

Gauḍaprakāśa
from Padmapurāṇa, Pātālakhaṇḍa; on Gauḍa Brahmans settled a. Gujarat during Vijayasim3ha Siddharāja's reign.
Pt.. with Gujarati transl. Baroda: Ahmedabad, 1899. See Br. Mus. Pt.. Bk.. 1892-1906. 502.

Gauḍatithitattva
or ºnibandha
Q. by Kāśīnātha in his Caṇḍikārcanadīpikā, RASB. VIII. A. 6405; by Śaṅkara Bhaṭṭa Ghāre in his Vratodyāpanakaumudī, BBRAS. 725; in Tithinirṇaya, Lz. 547; in Nāndīśrāddhaprayoga, RASB. III. 2348; in Rāmaprakāśa (compiled in the name of Kṛpārāma), IO. i. p. 503a; in Nirṇayasindhu an. Śūdradharmatattva, Mithilā.
C.. Tithitattva by Raghunandana.

Gauḍatripāṭhin_Bhagavat
a kāṇva; surnamed Vālmīki, father of Rudramaṇi Tripāṭhin, (a. of Ramalenduprakāśa, IO. 3130).

Gauḍadivyatattva
cited a. a. authority on law by Kamalākara Bhaṭṭa, in his Vivādatāṇḍava, IO. 1502. C.. Raghunandana's Tattvas.

Gauḍadvivedin
--Sampradāyadīpikā. Viśvabhāratī 1524.

Gauḍanibandha
cited a. a. authority by Rāmacandra in his Caturvim3śatimatavyākhyāna or Smṛtisaṅgraha(-ratna)vyākhyāna (?), a C. on the 1st ch. of the Caturvim3śatimata, IO. i. p. 476b; by Vidyāpati in his Durgābhaktitaraṅgiṇī or Durgotsavapaddhati, IO. [Page219-a. 2564; an. in Pitṛbhakti of Śrīdatta. See Kane, HDS. I. p. 543b.

Gauḍanibandhasāgara
prob. the Śrāddhasāgara of Kullūka Bhaṭṭa. mentioned in Nirṇayasindhu.
See Kane, HDS. I. p. 543b.

Gauḍapāda
adv. philosopher; traditionally considered a. the teacher of Govinda an. paramaguru of Śaṅkarācārya; the name Gauḍa suggests that he belonged to Bengal; Bhāvaviveka, in the first half of sixth Cent., q. verses from the Gauḍapāda Kārikās in his C. Tarkajvālā on his own Mādhyamikahṛdayakārikā, ch. VIII; an. influence of Nāgārjuna, Āryadeva an. Asaṅga is traced by scholars in his Kārikās; hence has to be assigned to the fifth Century A. D. See K. Kunjunni Raja, Adyar Library Bulletin, vol. XXIV. p. 130. Several legends are narrated about him in different works.
For general study on Gauḍapāda, see Dasgupta, His.. of Ind. Philosophy, Vol. I. p.. 423-9; Vidhusekhara Bhattacharya, Āgamaśāstra of Gauḍapāda, University of Calcutta, 1943; T. M. P. Mahadevan, Gauḍapāda, University of Madras, 1952; Gauḍapādakārikā, ed. with English Intro. an. translation by R. D. Karmarkar, BORI. 1953.
For a contrast between Śaṅkara an. Gauḍapāda see A. G. Krishna Warrier, ABORI. Golden Jubilee Vol. p.. 17-31.
On Gauḍapāda an. Buddhism see H. Jacobi, JAOS. 33. p.. 51-54; P. T. Raju, Gaudapada's Māṇḍukyakārikas. ABORI. 26. p.. 192-200.
Many of the works ascribed to Gauḍapāda are not by the a. of Māṇḍūkyakārikās. [Page219-b]
--Gauḍapādakārikās or Āgamaśāstra or Māṇḍūkyopaniṣatkārikās in 4 Prakaraṇas called (i) Āgamaprakaraṇa, (ii) Vaitathyaº, (iii) Advaitaº an. (iv) Alātaśantiº.
Pt.. Ānandāśrama 10.

--Śaktimīmām3sā or Gauḍapādasūtra or Śrīvidyāratnasūtra. Śāktāgama giving the mystic meaning of letters of Śrīvidyāmantra, deities represented by them an. the main principles of Śākta religion. MD. 5737. MT. 5159 (with C.). PUL. II. App. p. 61. TD. 15649. Whish 17b.

Gauḍavadha(gauḍavaho)
Pkt. kāvya composed in 700-725 A. D. by Vākpatirāja, son of Harṣadeva (acc. to Subhāṣitāvalī 3414); probably a student of Bhavabhūti (Gauḍavaho 799); patronised by King Yaśovarman of Kanauj (acc. to Kalhaṇa in Rājataraṅgiṇī, IV. 144); acc. to Jain legends Vākpati was thrown into prison where he composed the poem (See p.. CXXXVIII ff. Intro. S. P. Pandit's edn. of Gauḍavaho).
The extant text is inc. an. is a shorter version of the text.
BORI. 27 of 1873-74 (with C.). 17 of 1880-81. D. p. 165. Kh. Intro. p. v. 1284 (with C.). Pattan I. p.. 63. 294. 376 (with C.). 400 (select gāthās). Peters. I. App. p. 103 (no. 180. inc.).
For a ms. in Khatarvasī collection see ABORI. III. p. 47. [Page221-a.
Ed. S. P. Pandit, Bomb. Skt. & Pkt. Ser. 34 (with C. of Haripāla). First edn. 1887. 2nd edn. 1927.
See Wint. HIL. III. i. p. 92; WZKM. I. p. 324 ff., II. 328 ff; JRAS. 1908, p.. 765-78.
--C. on the current shorter version of text (G. v. sāra). by Hari(a)pāla(-lita), son of Upendra Bhaṭṭa; belonged to Jālandhara. A mere Skt. chāyā in most places.
BORI. 27 of 1873-74. Jesalmere p. 27. Kh. 84. Monatsber. Berl. Akad. 1874, 280. Pattan I. p. 376.
Pt.. in the edn. mentioned above, where see also Intro. p.. iv-x.
